name: PrepMedic (Sam Bonanno)
shortDescription: A critical-care flight paramedic explaining what a bystander can usefully do, and testing the emergency products sold on the promise that they help.
longDescription: The channel's own description states the credential — critical care flight paramedic, reserve deputy sheriff, tactical medic — and states the aim as evidence-based medical care for first responders and civilians alike. Two strands earn the listing. The first is bystander education proper: a thirty-three-minute treatment of six medications a bystander might encounter and what each actually does, a home paediatric choking kit, croup, what bystanders need to know when fire is involved. The second is more unusual and arguably more valuable: he tests emergency products against their marketing, including a viral haemostatic spray checked against the published science and several tourniquets tested rather than reviewed. That matters in a field where a device bought on a claim is a device you will trust when it counts. Be clear about the rest of the catalogue: a large share is tactical loadouts, chest rigs and medic bags aimed at professional responders and at an armed-civilian context that is specifically American.
notFor: Anyone wanting a structured first-aid syllabus, or anyone outside a US context — a substantial part of the catalogue assumes gunshot wounds, tactical kit and equipment that is not lawful or available everywhere. It is also not a substitute for a course.

categories.why: Bystander-level emergency education from someone qualified to give it, plus the rarer thing — emergency products tested against the claims they are sold on, which is what stops a kit being decoration.
categories.evidence: A thirty-three-minute explanation of six life-saving medications aimed explicitly at bystanders, a home paediatric choking kit, first aid and advanced care for croup, guidance for bystanders where fire is involved, and a fifteen-minute check of a viral haemostatic spray against the published science.

entryVideo.title: Could You Help? 6 Life-Saving Medications Explained for Bystanders
entryVideo.whyThisOne: It is aimed squarely at someone with no training who happens to be present, which is the situation this skill is actually about, and it explains rather than instructs.

caveats: **This is education, not training, and it cannot assess you.** First aid is acted on under pressure from memory, and certification exists because competence has to be checked by a person watching your hands — treat this as preparation for a course rather than a substitute. Much of the catalogue is tactical and gear-focused, heavily sponsored, and assumes a US armed-civilian context that does not transfer.
